Engine Room Records • Warm 1975 Folk-Rock Spirit

Songs from Cedar Run

Every evening once the hearth is banked, Sadie lifts Grandpa Owen Sawyer’s 1974 Clearwater steel-string guitar and all three triplets lock into warm, pastoral three-part harmonies in the spirit of mid-1970s acoustic storytellers.

Episode 1, Chapter 1 • Snowmelt and Red Cedar

Track 01: Cedar Run

Musical Feel: 1975 Pastoral Mountain Folk-Rock Ballad • Warm Analog Tape

Arrangement: Fingerpicked 6-string & shimmering 12-string acoustic guitars, rolling upright parlor piano, fretless bass, brushed snare, three-part sibling harmonies

Written after their very first silent night beyond the barbed-wire fence and their morning dip in the snowmelt granite pool—celebrating the nameless stream where nobody can split the three of them apart.

Read Matching Chapter →Visit The Listening Room →

Campfire Lyric Notebook

Eighteen summers screaming through the hallway and the floor Saying normal kids scatter when they reach an open door So we shouldered canvas rucksacks and Grandpa's old guitar Stepped across the back-fence wire beneath the evening star Carry me up to Cedar Run Where the cold spring meets the morning sun Three voices rising through the tall green pine No fence on the ridge, no dividing line
Sheltered Valley Rainstorms • All Three Footholds

Track 02: Rain on Split Cedar

Musical Feel: Mellow 1975 Acoustic Fingerpicking & Rain-Hush Harmony

Arrangement: Open-G Sitka spruce dreadnought guitar, soft wooden porch percussion, close twin-sister alto/soprano & brother baritone vocal blend

Captures why the triplets love afternoon rainstorms in Colville National Forest: cool rainwater splashing on upturned faces and steady white noise drumming overhead while they curl up dry together.

Read Matching Chapter →Visit The Listening Room →

Campfire Lyric Notebook

Let the gray cloud settle down the Kettle River draw Wash the sawdust off our knuckles, turn the pine duff soft and raw Every drop upon the roof-shakes is a wall against the past Just the white noise of the rainwater and peace that's built to last
Route 1 • The Creek-Bend Cedar Bench

Track 03: Straight Grain and Silver Water

Musical Feel: Sunny Mid-Tempo 1970s Acoustic Storyteller Groove

Arrangement: Twin steel-string guitars, warm upright bass, bright acoustic lead fills

Scored to the crisp crack of Grandpa Owen’s shingle froe splitting straight red heartwood and Tessa lifting silver-gold cutthroat trout from her woven willow trap.

Read Matching Chapter →Visit The Listening Room →

Campfire Lyric Notebook

Eighty feet of fallen heartwood seasoned ten years off the ground Every plank splits straight as music when the wooden maul comes down Willow basket in the riffle where the spotted cutthroat glide Supper sizzling on green alder with my sisters at my side
Route 2 • The South-Facing Granite Overhang

Track 04: Huckleberry Sun (Three Walls of Stone)

Musical Feel: Warm 1975 Canyon-Meadow Acoustic & Parlor Piano Ballad

Arrangement: Acoustic guitar arpeggios, warm upright piano chords, three-part chorus swell

Inspired by stained purple fingers in five acres of sunny mountain huckleberries and feeling the ancient granite cliff radiate stored daytime sunshine long after midnight.

Read Matching Chapter →Visit The Listening Room →

Campfire Lyric Notebook

Ten thousand tons of granite soaking June light all day long Breathing warmth back through the darkness like an ember in a song Purple berries on the flat rock, wild onion in the pot We got three walls built by glaciers and we love the roof we've got
Route 3 • The Forgotten Stone Springhouse

Track 05: Sixty Years Under the Moss

Musical Feel: Reflective 1975 High-Ridge Acoustic & Harmonica Waltz

Arrangement: 3/4 fingerpicked dreadnought guitar, gentle harmonica, soaring sibling harmonies

Sung beneath freshly peeled tamarack rafters atop the mossy 1930s fieldstone springhouse while forty-two-degree mountain water purls through the indoor stone trough.

Read Matching Chapter →Visit The Listening Room →

Campfire Lyric Notebook

Whoever laid these gable stones back in nineteen-thirty-three Left a doorway facing southward and a cold spring running free Sixty summers under feather-moss waiting on the hill For three kids to raise the ridgepole while the evening turns to still
Clear Midnight After Rain • Looking Up Together

Track 06: River of Stars Above the Pines

Musical Feel: Sweeping 1975 Nocturne • Cascading Piano & 12-String Shimmer

Arrangement: Cascading acoustic piano, 12-string guitar harmonics, sustained vocal harmonies echoing into quiet forest night

After a late rain washes every speck of pollen from the Kettle Range air, Luke, Tessa, and Sadie sit wrapped in one wool blanket watching the Milky Way reflect in Cedar Run.

Read Matching Chapter →Visit The Listening Room →

Campfire Lyric Notebook

Eighty miles from any streetlamp, after rain has washed the air There's an ocean made of starlight hanging silver up the stair Every world we used to dream of on a glowing living-room screen Shining real above the cedars in the deepest night we've seen
